chunks: And from him, from Muhammad al-Ash'ari, Abu Khallid, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zur'arah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The month of Ramadan is subject to the same increase and decrease [in days] that affects other months; so if the sky is overcast for a day, complete the count [to thirty days].

key_terms.الزِّيَادَةِ وَالنُّقْصَانِ: Increase and decrease (referring to the variation between 29 and 30 days)
key_terms.الْعِدَّةَ: The count/period (referring to the number of days)

ai.seo_question: How many days are in Ramadan if the moon is not seen due to clouds?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the mechanism of *ikmal* (completing the month to thirty days) when astronomical sighting is obstructed by clouds, a principle foundational to Shia fiqh regarding the lunar calendar. It underscores the flexibility of the Islamic calendar, aligning with the scholarly consensus that Ramadan is not fixed at thirty days but varies based on actual visibility, thereby preventing rigid adherence to a specific count when evidence is absent. This ruling highlights the practical application of *hujjiyyat al-akhbar* (reliability of traditions) in resolving minor discrepancies in timekeeping during the Prophet's and Imams' eras.
